data.outcome_summary: This TIMSS 2023 key-takeaways presentation summarizes international trends and equity-related patterns using TIMSS 2019 as the comparison point for achievement changes. It reports that, among 49 countries with comparable fourth-grade data, some countries show increases, some decreases, and some no change in both mathematics and science achievement; for eighth grade, only a small number of countries show increases in average mathematics and science achievement. The deck also highlights equity messages: high proportions of students reaching lower benchmarks, persistent links between home resources and achievement, and widening gender gaps favoring boys. It further reports absenteeism levels (e.g., around one-fifth of fourth graders absent at least once every two weeks, and higher rates at eighth grade) and links more positive attitudes toward mathematics/science with higher achievement. Because this is not an empirical methods report, no PV-combining, weighting, or model performance metrics are documented here.
